event: Battle of Ankara — Timur defeats Sultan Bayezid I, shattering Ottoman power and delaying the threat to Constantinople by decades
Ottoman Interregnum begins — Bayezid's sons war for succession, fragmenting the empire into rival sultanates
Mehmed I reunifies the Ottoman Empire after defeating his brothers, ending the interregnum
Murad II becomes Sultan — begins rebuilding Ottoman military power and turning attention back toward Constantinople
First Ottoman siege of Constantinople under Murad II — the walls hold but the empire's vulnerability is exposed
Thessalonica sold to Venice — the Byzantines cannot defend their second city and hand it to a trading power
Fall of Thessalonica to the Ottomans — Venice loses the city after seven years, population massacred or enslaved
Council of Florence — Byzantine Emperor John VIII agrees to union of Eastern and Western churches in exchange for military aid that never materializes
Ottoman siege of Belgrade repelled by Hungarian forces under John Hunyadi
Crusade of Varna launched — Hungarian, Polish, and Wallachian forces march against the Ottomans
Battle of Varna — Crusader army destroyed, King Władysław III killed. Last serious Western attempt to save Constantinople fails
Ottoman devastation of the Morea — Byzantine despotate in the Peloponnese ravaged, Hexamilion wall destroyed
Second Battle of Kosovo — Hunyadi defeated again. Ottoman control of the Balkans is now uncontested
Mehmed II becomes Sultan at age 19 — immediately begins planning the conquest of Constantinople
Rumeli Hisarı fortress constructed on the Bosphorus — Mehmed II cuts Constantinople's Black Sea supply line
Venetian and Genoese communities in Constantinople debate whether to fight or negotiate — the city's Italian quarters are divided
Siege of Constantinople begins — Mehmed II's army of 80,000 surrounds the city with the largest cannon ever built
qid_note: Q105765 covers both siege and fall — this entry is the siege phase

event: Fall of Constantinople — the city falls on May 29. Emperor Constantine XI dies fighting. The Byzantine Empire ends after 1,100 years
qid_note: Distinct from siege entry — null QID to avoid dedup with Q105765

event: Greek scholars flee to Italy carrying manuscripts — accelerating the Italian Renaissance and the transmission of classical knowledge
Constantinople's population has fallen below 50,000 — once a city of half a million, it is now a collection of villages inside ancient walls
